newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel cargoes flat, dull but ARA barges gain $1.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel cargoes flat, dull but ARA barges gain $1.

text.p: NWE fuel was little changed on Monday despite a $1 gain on Rotterdam barges which caught up with late Friday gains on Brent crude.
But activity was thin and demand from end-users in Portugal and Italy was subdued.

After early gains of up to $2 a tonne on Rotterdam barges, prices slipped back slightly during the afternoon. Towards the close talk was pegged around $113 after trade in the range $112 to $114 soon after the open.
On cargoes a prompt Scandinavian cargo was shown around $107 fob but drew scant interest, while at least one trader was heard
Russian exports remain scarce apart from about three straight-run E-4 cargoes which look likely to be snapped up by refiners for gas oil production.

Low sulphur was quiet but talked around $121 fob for mid-October loading. This compares to low sulphur straight-run cargoes which dipped to about $125 fob on Friday but talked nearer $127 on early on Monday.
A Turkish tender for a 45,00-tonne low sulphur cracked cargo was heard awarded at $11.50 above the fob mean quotes.
